title: 2022 AMC 10A Problem 5
statement: Square \(ABCD\) has side length \(1.\) Points \(P,\) \(Q,\) \(R,\) and \(S\) each lie on a side of \(ABCD\) such that \(APQCRS\) is an equilateral convex hexagon with side length \(s.\) What is \(s?\)

solutions.text:
Consider the diagram:

Since \(AP = QC = s,\) we know that \(PB = BQ.\) This shows that \(\triangle PBQ\) is an isosceles right triangle with hypotenuse \(PQ=s.\) Using the Pythagorean theorem, we get that \(PB = \dfrac{s}{\sqrt{2}}.\)

We also know that \[ 1 = AB = AP + PB = s + \dfrac{s}{\sqrt{2}}. \]

This equation simplifies to \[ 1 = (1 + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}})s \] Which implies that \[ s = \dfrac{1}{1 + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2} + 1}. \]

We can rationalize this fraction to get

\[ \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2} + 1} \cdot \dfrac{\sqrt{2} - 1}{\sqrt{2} - 1} = 2 - \sqrt{2}. \]

Thus, C is the correct answer.
hints: Use the \(45\)–\(45\)–\(90\) triangle at a corner of the square
Write the side of the square as one hexagon side plus one corner leg
